In $△OPR$ shown above, we have 

- $OP=3|p|$

- $\overset{\to }{OP}$ has the opposite direction to $p$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OP}=-3p.$

Similarly:

- $PR=2|q|$

- $\overset{\to }{PR}$ has the opposite direction to $q$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PR}=-2q.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PR} \\  & =-3p-2q.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $r=\lambda p+\mu q=-3p-2q.$

Since $p∦q,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =-3$ and $\mu =-2$

Consider the picture above. Given that $c=\lambda a+3b,$ find $\lambda .$
questions.worked_solution:
To find $\lambda ,$ we want to match the expression

$$
c=\lambda a+3b.
$$

We are given that one of the components is $3b.$ So, we first draw the vector $3b$ from the origin. Then we complete the path to the point $C.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14258034/assets/52421034c2919620a0a9aae844db0eba2d396e5d6f1152d69bee40ff56c4d8ad.png)

Let $P$ be the endpoint of the vector $3b.$ Then

$$
c=\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC}.
$$

In $△OPC,$ we have:

- $PC=3|a|$

- $\overset{\to }{PC}$ and $a$ have opposite directions

Hence, $\overset{\to }{PC}=-3a.$

Additionally,

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =\overset{\to }{OP}+\overset{\to }{PC} \\  & =3b-3a.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $c=\lambda a+3b=-3a+3b.$

Since $a∦b,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients of $a,$ we get:

$$
\lambda =-3
$$

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OC}=c,$ $\overset{\to }{OR}=r,$ and $X$ divides $\overset{―}{CR}$ in the ratio $CX:XR=6:11.$ Express $\overset{\to }{OX}$ via the vectors $c$ and $r.$

$\,\overset{\to }{OX}=$
{{field-1}}
$c+$
{{field-2}}
$r$
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OX}=\overset{\to }{OC}+\overset{\to }{CX}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OC}=c,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{CX}.$

First, from $△OCR,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CR} & =\overset{\to }{CO}+\overset{\to }{OR} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OC}+\overset{\to }{OR} \\  & =-c+r \\  & =r-c.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $CX:XR=6:11,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{CX}=\frac{6}{17}\overset{\to }{CR}=\frac{6}{17}(r-c).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OX} & =\overset{\to }{OC}+\overset{\to }{CX} \\  & =c+\frac{6}{17}(r-c) \\  & =\frac{11}{17}c+\frac{6}{17}r.\end{aligned}
$$
